evidence.exact_quote: All `/goal` prompts must stay under 4,000 characters. Replace placeholders before use.

items.impact: Users are told the hard size constraint, but no check proves a substituted prompt remains below the limit; long feature names, ledger ids, or localized text can silently make a prompt invalid.
items.statement: The prompt catalog establishes a 4,000-character ceiling and placeholder substitution duty without defining a measurable post-substitution validation step or failure response.
items.title: Prompt length limit lacks an executable oracle

evidence.exact_quote: Create a new v2 ledger under Plans/ledgers/v2/ with ledger_id pldg-YYYYMMDD-NNN-<slug>. Register it in Plans/ledgers/v2/ledger_registry.json.

items.impact: A new conversational feature has an explicit storage location, identifier pattern, and registry side effect.
items.statement: The start prompt creates and registers a v2 ledger before conversational design proceeds.
items.title: Conversational ledger creation is explicitly routed

evidence.exact_quote: This is a conversational design/spec thread, not a Goal run. Do not write canonical Plans yet. Use the $pm-bootstrap-planning-ledger skill if available.

items.impact: Ordinary specification conversation cannot mutate canonical product Plans, keeping planning memory and canon separated.
items.statement: The document clearly denies canonical-write authority to the conversational start lane.
items.title: Conversational and canonical write authority are separated

evidence.exact_quote: After each substantive turn, update events.jsonl, touched records/*.jsonl, and state/current.json, state/handoff.json, state/open_items.json, state/compile_queue.json.

items.impact: A crash or competing writer between updates can leave event history, records, and projections mutually inconsistent, with no prescribed repair, transaction boundary, lock, or idempotent replay rule.
items.statement: The start workflow requires a coordinated multi-file state transition but does not define update ordering, atomicity, concurrency control, failure recovery, or rollback.
items.title: Ledger projection updates have no atomicity contract

evidence.exact_quote: Preserve exact tokens, examples, negative constraints, stale/retired terms, compatibility-only notes, owner hints, and user corrections. Keep open questions explicit.

items.impact: Exact preservation can propagate secrets, personal data, hostile instructions, or unsafe payloads from user-provided content into durable ledger and later canonical artifacts because no quarantine, classification, escaping, or redaction boundary is defined.
items.statement: Lossless preservation is strong for semantic fidelity but lacks a safety and data-lifecycle policy for untrusted or sensitive tokens.
items.title: Exact-token preservation lacks trust and privacy controls

evidence.exact_quote: Automatically classify every design atom as gui_related true or false. Mark true for GUI/UI/screens/pages/panels/forms/layout/styling/components/icons/SVGs/images/screenshots/user-visible visual presentation. The user does not need to label GUI work.

items.impact: Every atom carries an explicit machine-usable GUI classification and the system, not the user, owns the classification burden.
items.statement: The start prompt defines a binary GUI-truth field and enumerates visible presentation categories that require true.
items.title: GUI-related classification is mandatory and inferred

evidence.exact_quote: Do not read full events.jsonl, source shards, or legacy working_ledger.md unless a state file points to a specific source_ref that must be inspected.

items.impact: Resume work is bounded to compact state and only expands to detailed lineage on a concrete reference, controlling context size and avoiding indiscriminate legacy reads.
items.statement: The continue prompt imposes a compact-state-first read boundary with explicit source-ref escalation.
items.title: Continuation uses bounded compact-state intake

evidence.exact_quote: Continue from the cursor. After each substantive turn, update the ledger and handoff state. Infer gui_related true/false for every new or changed design atom; do not ask me to label GUI work.

items.impact: A missing, stale, conflicting, or invalid cursor can cause replay, omission, or continuation from the wrong state because precedence, validation, and repair behavior are not defined.
items.statement: Continuation assumes a usable cursor without specifying its identity, allowed states, consistency check against registry/current/handoff, or failure path.
items.title: Cursor resume semantics are underspecified

evidence.exact_quote: - Ledger is source/planning memory, not canon.

items.impact: Builders have no discretion to treat ledger prose as canonical product truth; accepted content must be compiled into owner docs.
items.statement: The compilation lane explicitly assigns source-memory status to the ledger and canonical authority to live Plans.
items.title: Ledger authority is explicitly non-canonical

evidence.exact_quote: - Never use source_preserving_planunit for new feature content or new owner-doc creation; that mode is only for lossless legacy Plan conversion.

items.impact: Legacy-lossless representation cannot leak into newly authored feature canon or owner-doc creation.
items.statement: The source-preserving profile has an explicit compatibility-only scope.
items.title: Legacy conversion mode is barred from new content

evidence.exact_quote: - If owner placement is ambiguous, record candidate owners and adjudication evidence; do not ask row-by-row.

items.impact: Candidate recording prevents interruption but does not say who decides, what evidence is sufficient, or whether unresolved ownership blocks compilation, allowing inconsistent routing across builders.
items.statement: Ambiguous owner placement has a recording rule but no deterministic adjudicator, completion oracle, or escalation threshold.
items.title: Owner ambiguity has no closure contract

evidence.exact_quote: - Do not create WorkNodes or executable build tasks.

items.impact: Compilation cannot cross into executable planning or runtime work generation.
items.statement: The ledger-to-Plans compiler lane has a clear non-executable boundary.
items.title: Plan compilation cannot emit build work

evidence.exact_quote: 3. Build a coverage map proving every original span maps to a standardized section, PlanUnit, preserved appendix/source block, or explicit disposition.

items.impact: Every original span must have an explicit destination or disposition, making omission detectable during migration.
items.statement: Lossless standardization requires a complete span-level coverage proof before broad conversion.
items.title: Migration fidelity has a span-coverage oracle

evidence.exact_quote: 6. Continue in controlled batches only after pilot passes.

items.impact: Large migrations can proceed with inconsistent batch sizes and no prescribed checkpoint, rollback, retry, or recovery behavior after a later batch partially fails.
items.statement: Pilot gating is explicit, but controlled batch sizing and post-pilot failure recovery remain undefined.
items.title: Controlled migration batches lack operational semantics

evidence.exact_quote: Assign gui_related true/false to every PlanUnit by inference. Split mixed GUI/backend units when safe; otherwise mark gui_related=true and note split_recommended.

items.impact: Mixed units cannot be falsely classified as backend-only; unsafe splits preserve GUI visibility and surface future normalization work.
items.statement: The migration prompt defines conservative GUI classification for inseparable mixed units.
items.title: Mixed GUI units fail safe to gui_related true

evidence.exact_quote: - Approve And Build remains disabled unless Plans/.implementation_readiness/buildability_gate_report.json reports buildability_gate_passed=true.

items.impact: The visible build action cannot be enabled by mere plan capture, indexing, schemas, semantic closure, or passing validators.
items.statement: Approve And Build has a single explicit enabling oracle tied to the implementation-readiness report.
items.title: Build enablement is fail-closed on the readiness gate

evidence.exact_quote: Produce generated outputs under Plans/.plan_index/:

items.impact: The output filenames are enumerated, but producer schemas, versioning, atomic publication, and downstream consumers are not identified here, so incompatible or partially updated indexes may still appear complete.
items.statement: The index prompt names artifacts without specifying their caller/consumer bindings or publication compatibility contract.
items.title: Plan index outputs lack consumer and publication contracts

evidence.exact_quote: Read AGENTS.md, Plans/Plan_Document_System.md, Plans/Plan_To_Node_Compilation.md, and live Plans docs. Do not alter canonical prose unless a small repair is required and clearly validated.

items.impact: A generator can modify canonical prose based on subjective judgments about size and validation, expanding a generated-index task into an uncontrolled authoring lane.
items.statement: The index lane grants conditional canonical-write authority without a bound on repair scope, authorized files, evidence, approval, or rollback.
items.title: Small canonical repairs are not objectively bounded

evidence.exact_quote: - If Plans are incomplete, set node_readiness_report.status = blocked_plans_incomplete.

items.impact: When Plans are incomplete and runtime is disabled simultaneously, different builders may emit different single statuses and users may see a misleading primary reason.
items.statement: The readiness report defines blocked_plans_incomplete and runtime_disabled conditions but no precedence or multi-condition representation.
items.title: Node-readiness status conflicts have no resolution rule

evidence.exact_quote: 6. Produce final certification with changed files, validators, blockers, and unresolved risks.

items.impact: Operators receive a bounded record of mutations, checks, blockers, and residual risk after governance sealing.
items.statement: Governance seal completion includes an explicit operational certification surface.
items.title: Governance sealing requires observable certification

evidence.exact_quote: 2. Regenerate generated shards/evidence/plan graph artifacts using repo scripts.

items.impact: Failure between regeneration, Spec Lock refresh, decision updates, and full gates can leave a mixed governance generation with no mandated cleanup, rollback, or resumable checkpoint.
items.statement: Governance sealing is a multi-stage mutation pipeline without atomic publication or partial-failure recovery semantics.
items.title: Governance seal lacks transactional recovery

evidence.exact_quote: Input: ledger_id=infer_latest. Audit-only. Do not edit Plans, ledgers, .plan_index, governance, code, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, queues, manifests, implementation files, or build tasks. Write only Plans/.audits/<audit_id>/*.

items.impact: Closed-world auditing cannot alter the subject, generated index, governance, runtime artifacts, or implementation; evidence is isolated to the audit directory.
items.statement: The semantic audit lane has a comprehensive read-only subject boundary and a single output namespace.
items.title: Closed-world audit writes are tightly isolated

evidence.exact_quote: Before semantic review, build audit_scope_manifest.jsonl with deterministic chk check_id rows for every compiled atom detail, compile target, added/changed PlanUnit claim, reciprocal source_lineage claim, owner/consumer route, schema/contract identity, depends_on/unblocks edge, ledger projection field, index/governance check, and forbidden-artifact check. Rows carry refs, source_atom_ids, plan_unit_ids, owner_docs, detail_keys, exact_tokens, covered_artifacts, classification, repair_required, and finding_level. Completion requires 100% classified rows.

items.impact: Semantic completion is falsifiable against an exhaustive, deterministic scope inventory rather than inferred from a small set of findings or validator success.
items.statement: The audit requires deterministic check rows across atom, PlanUnit, lineage, routing, contract, graph, projection, governance, and forbidden-artifact surfaces, with total classification.
items.title: Closed-world scope has an exhaustive classification oracle

evidence.exact_quote: Read registry before emitting risks. If a finding is closed and hashes/evidence match, classify previously_closed with repair_required=false and write closure_reuse.jsonl, not a new semantic risk. Reopen only on changed source/PlanUnit/owner/closure hashes or blocked/reopened status.

items.impact: Stable closed evidence is reused without generating duplicate risks, while defined hash or status changes permit reopening.
items.statement: Finding lifecycle transitions are gated by closure evidence identity and explicit changed-hash or status conditions.
items.title: Closure reuse and reopen transitions are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Infer observation_ref=HEAD. Infer subject_ref as latest substantive commit touching live Plans, target-ledger governing state, .plan_index, governance, or process scripts; exclude Plans/.audits/**, closure-registry-only commits, and hygiene-only report edits. Infer ledger_id from latest non-background registry/recent commits, audit_id=next audit-YYYYMMDD-NNN-<slug>, and baseline_ref from the parent of the earliest contiguous subject cycle commit.

items.impact: Concurrent commits or multiple recent ledgers can change HEAD during the audit and make latest, substantive, non-background, contiguous, or next ambiguous, yielding non-repeatable refs or audit-id collisions.
items.statement: Audit ref and identity inference lacks a frozen-snapshot step, deterministic tie-breakers, and collision handling.
items.title: Latest-cycle inference is vulnerable to races and ambiguity

evidence.exact_quote: BLOCKED only when repair_required=true, a validator fails/mutates state, forbidden artifacts exist, or a user decision is required. PASS_WITH_WARNINGS is terminal when all findings are repair_required=false. PASS means no findings.

items.impact: Status cannot be inflated to PASS or incorrectly blocked by non-actionable observations; validator mutation is explicitly treated as failure.
items.statement: The audit defines mutually meaningful terminal statuses from actionable findings, validator behavior, forbidden artifacts, and user decisions.
items.title: Audit terminal status semantics are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Scan audit artifacts for repair_required=true. If count is zero, no-op: do not edit Plans, ledgers, governance, registry, repair_closure_matrix.jsonl, repair_impact_matrix.jsonl, or prior audit artifacts; report PASS_WITH_WARNINGS terminal or PASS terminal from the audit.

items.impact: A repair request with no actionable rows cannot churn canonical, governance, registry, closure, impact, or historical audit artifacts.
items.statement: The repair lane has an explicit no-op terminal transition when actionable finding count is zero.
items.title: Zero-action repair is safely terminal and mutation-free

evidence.exact_quote: Before editing, write repair_impact_matrix.jsonl. Map every actionable finding to files, PlanUnits, schemas, dependency_edges, owner_refs, ledger_projection_fields, index_artifacts, governance_artifacts, scope_check_ids, and post_repair_semantic_audit placeholder. Then repair only mapped impact surfaces. Do not revalidate previously_closed, exact_present, equivalent_with_evidence, ordinary validator warnings, audit-artifact wording, or repair_required=false observations. Audit-only observation/hygiene repairs do not stale/restamp ledger latest_audit_*.

items.impact: Repairs cannot silently broaden to unmapped files, graph edges, projections, index, governance, or non-actionable observations.
items.statement: Every actionable repair must have a pre-edit impact map across direct and propagated surfaces, and edits are limited to that map.
items.title: Repair propagation is bounded by an impact matrix

evidence.exact_quote: Run an internal post-repair semantic audit over the original audit_scope_manifest.jsonl plus every impact row. If new repair_required findings appear, add them to the same scope/impact set and repair/adjudicate in this Goal. Iterate until repair_required_count=0 or a true user decision blocks. Passing validators alone are insufficient.

items.impact: Repair closure is tested against original and propagated scope and cannot be claimed merely from green validators.
items.statement: The repair lane requires iterative semantic closure to zero actionable findings or a genuine user-decision block.
items.title: Post-repair semantic closure is mandatory

evidence.exact_quote: For compile, audit, and repair prompts, use bounded read-only subagents when atom, owner-doc, or document-size thresholds are exceeded; require assignment/result evidence and keep the main agent as sole writer. Deep audit must cover atom fidelity, reciprocal lineage, owner routing, changed-doc fidelity, ledger consistency, index/governance status, forbidden artifacts, and validator mutability. Repair must write closure rows only for repair_required=true findings, no-op when none exist, and must not treat passing validators alone as semantic closure when actionable rows remain. PlanUnit indexing remains non-executable, and governance seal validates the target ledger only after Plans and indexes are stable.

items.impact: Agents cannot determine consistently when to shard, how many workers are bounded, how to prevent overlapping assignments, or what to do with missing, conflicting, stale, or malformed result evidence; the sole writer can become a throughput and recovery bottleneck.
items.statement: The hardening addendum mandates read-only delegation with evidence and a sole writer, but leaves thresholds, partition identity, concurrency limits, retry, conflict detection, and partial-result recovery unspecified.
items.title: Subagent scaling lacks dispatch and recovery contracts

evidence.exact_quote: - Every indexed PlanUnit must include gui_related true/false.

items.impact: A unit can be correctly labeled GUI-related while omitting accessibility and localization requirements entirely; downstream index and readiness consumers cannot distinguish that omission from completed GUI truth.
items.statement: The binary gui_related field provides routing truth but the prompt catalog contains no accessibility or localization capture, validation, or readiness contract for those units.
items.title: GUI classification does not cover accessibility or localization

evidence.exact_quote: - Run safe plan validators before claiming success.

items.impact: Validator or workflow dependency failures caused by offline state, missing tools, permissions, or transient I/O can be confused with plan defects or ignored, because classification, retry, and degraded-mode behavior are absent.
items.statement: The prompts require safe validation but do not define behavior when required tooling or external/environmental dependencies are unavailable.
items.title: Offline and environment failure handling is unspecified

evidence.exact_quote: Audit latest PM Bootstrap Ledger-to-Plans cycle for closed-world semantic fidelity and terminal state.

items.impact: The audit is deliberately scoped to repository-contained semantic evidence rather than allowing external material to silently redefine canonical truth.
items.statement: Closed-world fidelity is an explicit audit property; lack of external research in this lane is intentional, not an accidental omission.
items.title: Semantic audit intentionally uses a closed world

segments.summary: Reviewed all 241 lines defining the PM Bootstrap prompt lifecycle from conversational ledger creation and continuation through compilation, lossless standardization, PlanUnit indexing, governance sealing, restart audit, closed-world semantic audit, bounded repair, and the compile-hardening addendum. Exact strengths include explicit authority boundaries, GUI classification, lossless coverage, fail-closed build readiness, exhaustive semantic scope, closure reuse, terminal status semantics, no-op repair, impact mapping, and semantic post-repair closure. Adversarial gaps center on multi-file atomicity, untrusted-content handling, resume validation, ownership adjudication, batch rollback, generated-artifact consumers, canonical-repair authority, status precedence, seal recovery, latest-cycle races, subagent dispatch recovery, accessibility/localization, and offline/tool failure behavior.

cross_document_questions: Which canonical owner defines atomic multi-file ledger projection updates, cursor validation, writer locking, and replay or rollback after partial failure?
Where are schemas, versioning, atomic publication rules, and downstream consumers defined for every Plans/.plan_index and implementation-readiness artifact?
Which owner defines deterministic precedence when blocked_plans_incomplete and runtime_disabled are simultaneously true?
Which canonical contracts define governance-seal checkpoints, rollback, validator mutation handling, and safe resume after partial regeneration?
Where are the objective delegation thresholds, disjoint assignment identity, concurrency limits, evidence validation, retry, and conflict handling defined for bounded read-only subagents?
Which owner makes accessibility and localization requirements mandatory and readiness-testable for gui_related PlanUnits?
Where is the policy for secrets, personal data, prompt injection, and other untrusted exact tokens before they are durably preserved or compiled?
research_queries: atomic crash-consistent multi-file projection patterns for append-only event ledgers
deterministic work sharding and result attestation protocols for read-only audit agents
safe exact-token preservation policies for secrets personal data and prompt injection
transactional publication and rollback for generated governance artifact sets
accessibility and localization readiness criteria for UI-linked planning units
